newsitem.title: UK: IRA says British police shot unarmed man.
newsitem.headline: IRA says British police shot unarmed man.

text.p: Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, has accused British police of shooting an unarmed man who died when they seized arms and explosives during raids in London on Monday.
Diarmuid O'Neil, 27, was killed and five other men were arrrested following the capture of 10 tonnes of arms and explosives, the biggest seizure ever made in Britain.
Sinn Fein claimed that "no exchange of fire took place" during the raids.

"Once more the security services have used the tactic of feeding disinformation to the media to cover up their shoot first and then make up the facts policy," Sinn Fein vice president Pat Doherty said.
"The admission this evening that no exchange of fire took place is in direct contradiction to the stories fed to a gullible press over the past 36 hours.

"These inspired leaks started with a gun battle, then an exchange of fire and finally to the admission that these were no more than a calculated attempt by the British security services to cover up their deliberate shooting of Dermot O'Neill rather than effect his arrest."
A police spokesman refused to comment on the claims and said that the Police Complaints Authority was dealing with the matter.
But the Daily Mail newspaper said police chiefs were ready for a backlash over the incident although they were confident that all the officers involved had acted properly.
"There would only have been a split second to react as they burst in on a man they believed was armed and highly dangerous," the newspaper said.
The suspects can be detained for a week without charge under anti-terrorism laws brought in to combat the IRA's guerrilla activities.
One of the five men being questioned by police in London is a young Northern Irish British Airways engineer working at Britain's Gatwick airport.

Police hailed the seizure as a major blow to the IRA's 25-year war against British rule in Northern Ireland and said they believed the IRA was within hours of launching lorry bomb attacks and targeting high profile public figures.
Police in Ireland swooped on several homes near the border with British-ruled Northern Ireland early on Tuesday but no arrests were made.
Monday's events dashed hopes that the IRA, which broke it's 17-month ceasefire with a bomb in London in February that killed two people, would call a new truce.
Sinn Fein has been barred from all-party peace talks on the province until the IRA agrees to lay down its arms.
